instructions: At least 1 hour ahead, or the night before: grate the garlic into a large bowl. Add the tomato paste, the olive oil, the paprika, the thyme, the salt and the pepper and stir into a thick paste.
Pat the chicken thighs dry. Add them to the bowl and rub the paste all over each one, under the skin too. Cover and refrigerate.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment and set the thighs on it skin side up, with space between them.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and the tops are browned in spots.

Meanwhile, rinse the rice, then bring 3 cups of water to a boil in a medium pot. Add the rice and 1/2 tsp salt, cover, and cook on low for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork. Chop 1/4 cup of the parsley.

You're cooking the chicken to 175°F at the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest thigh: it's done when the juices run clear and there's no pink left.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes, then spoon the juices from the tray over it.
Taste a piece of the chicken. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt.
Scatter the parsley over the chicken and serve with the rice.
method_notes: Yemek.com's Tavuk Pirzola (the lead, 4.2 from 23 ratings) rubs bone-in thighs with a yogurt, olive oil, garlic, red pepper and thyme paste, marinates at least an hour and bakes them. A second yemek.com version uses tomato paste, yogurt and cumin and cooks in a pan. The yogurt is replaced with tomato paste from the second version to keep it dairy-free, the oven is set hotter than the lead's 356°F so it fits the time, and the red pepper is paprika to keep the base mild. The list line mentions a pepper paste, which neither version uses.
advance_prep_notes: marinate at least 1 hour ahead (or overnight)
